newsitem.title: USA: Dover extends, amends rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Dover extends, amends rights plan.

text.p: Dover Corp said on Friday its board of directors amended its shareholder rights plan, originally adopted in November 1987, extending it and altering some of the original features.
The plan was extended until November 2006, the intitial exercise price was increased and the stock ownership threshold of an acquiring person was reduced.

Under the amended plan, each shareholder would have one right attached to each share of outstanding common stock, the company said. The right would now entitle the holder to purchase one four-thousandth of a share of Series A Junior Participating Preferred Stock at an initial exercise price of $200, the company said.
Initially, rights were attached to the company's common stock and were not exercisable, Dover said.

But they become exercisable after any person or group acquired beneficial ownership of 15 percent or more of the Company's common stock, or 10 days after any person or group announces a tender or exchange offer that would result in that same beneficial ownership level, Dover said.
